The core challenge is aligning 3D human meshes across abrupt camera changes while preserving individual identities. We formulate this as a constrained optimization problem. Let \(M_i^t\) be the mesh of person \(i\) at frame \(t\). Under a shared 3D space \(\mathcal{S}\), we minimize the reprojection error \(E_{reproj} = \sum_{i,t} \| \pi(T_i^t M_i^t) - \hat{x}_i^t \|^2\) subject to identity consistency constraints \(I(M_i^{t_b-1}) = I(M_i^{t_b+1})\) across the shot boundary \(t_b\). The identity map \(I\) ensures the same person is tracked. Joint trajectory smoothing adds a temporal regularization term \(E_{smooth} = \lambda \sum_{i,t} \| M_i^{t+1} - M_i^t \|^2\). Solving this yields globally consistent 3D trajectories.
